UN General Assembly Votes to Promote Equal Earth Projection for More Accurate World Maps

2026-09-07 Reyyan Dogan, ArchDaily UN, Equal Earth projection, Mercator, world map, cartographic representation, equal-area projection, architecture, education, Togo, African Union
Read the source article

Quick summary

The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to promote equal-area map projections like Equal Earth, encouraging governments, schools, and tech companies to represent continents at their true relative sizes rather than the distorted Mercator view used since the 16th century.

Key takeaways

  • The UN General Assembly voted on September 4, 2026, with 164 in favor, 1 against, and 6 abstentions to promote equal-area world map projections
  • The resolution was sponsored by Togo and encourages governments, educational institutions, international organizations, and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections
  • The 2018 Equal Earth projection is identified as an example of a map that accurately represents continental scale
  • The resolution does not formally replace or prohibit the Mercator projection, which has been used since the 16th century
  • It calls for education about the limitations of representing Earth's curved surface on a two-dimensional map
  • The resolution is non-binding but could influence cartographic standards in education and digital mapping
